title: Shopping Cart
statement:
Tony is visiting a supermarket to buy Z cans of coke. The supermarket offers only two types of packs:

- A pack of 2 cans costs X dollars.
- A pack of 4 cans costs Y dollars.

Tony can purchase any number of these packs. He is allowed to buy more than Z cans if necessary, but he cannot buy individual cans.

For each test case, determine the minimum total cost required to purchase at least Z cans.

examples.explanation:
Test Case 1: Five 2-packs → 10 cans → Cost = 25.
Test Case 2: Two 4-packs + One 2-pack → 10 cans → Cost = 21.
Test Case 3: One 4-pack + One 2-pack → 6 cans → Cost = 11.

hints: Hint 1: Check if buying 4-packs is cheaper per can than buying 2-packs (i.e. Y < 2 * X).
Hint 2: If Y >= 2 * X, 2-packs are always strictly cheaper or equal per can, so buy ceil(Z / 2) two-packs.
Hint 3: If Y < 2 * X, buy as many 4-packs as possible (Z // 4). Handle the remainder (0, 1, 2, or 3 cans) by comparing one more 4-pack vs one 2-pack.
discussion: Compare the cost of full 4-packs and optimal combinations for remaining cans.
